sampling_model.design: Three-arm randomized experiment with known assignment probabilities \(\pi_d\).
sampling_model.units: Independent units with the potential efficacy and toxicity components mapped by \(\text{def:prespecified-benefit-risk-score}\) to an ordinal response triple supported on \(\mathcal U_L\).
sampling_model.treatment: Observed dose \(A\in\{0,1,2\}\) and observed prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score \(Y=Y(A)\).
sampling_model.overlap: \(\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\pi_d>0\), with realized empty arms handled by the exact fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Arm-specific multinomial probabilities \(p_{dj}\) are estimated by randomized-arm empirical frequencies. Their fixed-\(L\) endpoint plug-ins have error \(O_P((N\pi_{\min})^{-1/2})\); exact simultaneous inference instead conditions on realized main-sample arm counts, uses a pilot product-simplex region, and returns full logical ranges for required empty arms.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Discrete causal bounds can be computed as polynomial programs with convergent anytime outer bounds.
Finite causal response-type models can have complete observable facet inequalities beyond Pearl's basic instrumental inequality.
A deterministic parent map supports duplicate-free reverse-search enumeration without storing visited objects.

Two-arm ordinal benefit probabilities have sharp cumulative formulas for unrestricted bivariate potential-outcome couplings; those formulas do not transfer sharply to the three-way non-valley support restriction.
Two-potential-outcome distributional bounds under support restrictions admit a Kantorovich-dual characterization.

Unrestricted multiple-potential-outcome identification admits a multi-marginal transport formulation, with a plug-in rate for the paper's quadratic objective; without an extended-cost constrained reduction it gives only inclusion-based outer bounds for the present forbidden-support indicator target.
General potential-response support restrictions have sharp graph-based observable implications, with extra inequalities in nonregular cases.
Randomly perturbed LP value functions yield uniformly valid confidence sets for linear functionals of set-identified parameters.
For Gaussian first-stage limits, ordinary bootstrap consistency is equivalent to full differentiability, and a derivative-estimation bootstrap handles directional maps.
Intersection bounds admit adaptive inequality selection and Gaussian-process inference.
Continuous functionals of the joint distribution of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model admit sharp bounds through random-set restrictions and convex optimization.

For binary treatment and an ordinal outcome, exact randomization inference in the paper assumes independent potential outcomes and concerns the relative treatment effect, not the present three-dose unique-best endpoint map.

Sharp symbolic ordinal bounds are derived for binary-exposure observational confounding and binary-instrument noncompliance designs; they do not classify or evaluate a three-dose forbidden-support unique-best polytope.

body.tldr: Randomization identifies the three arm marginals of a prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score, while weak individual unimodality restricts the latent three-way coupling used to define unique-best-dose shares. For every fixed ordinal support, each sharp scalar endpoint now has both a sparse canonical-facet formula using at most three normals and a direct support-constrained finite transport dual with an exact five-region prefix/suffix separator; therefore scalar endpoint computation does not require the unresolved all-\(L\) facet stream. The endpoint maps are globally Lipschitz finite maxima or minima of affine contrasts, giving plug-in error \(O_P((N\pi_{\min})^{-1/2})\). A pilot-split least-favourable conditional-multinomial construction gives exact simultaneous finite-sample coverage with empty-arm, zero-cell, and tie fallbacks. Regular-face equivalence to an efficient Wald interval remains open, as does the sound, complete, unique bounded-register all-support facet stream.

project_justification.gap: Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) give sharp formulas and attaining tables for unrestricted bivariate ordinal potential-outcome couplings, so their result has no automatic sharp transfer to a three-way coupling after strict-middle-valley triples are deleted. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) provide unrestricted multi-marginal identification and a rate theorem for a quadratic objective; inclusion alone gives at most outer bounds for the present constrained indicator objective unless an extended-cost support reduction is proved, and their quadratic rate is not imported here. Chiba's exact randomization inference assumes independent potential outcomes and concerns the relative treatment effect. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) treat binary-exposure confounding and binary-instrument noncompliance designs. None supplies the present legal-response incidence dual, three-normal necessity witness, complete all-support facet grammar, or exact support-aware six-endpoint construction.
project_justification.niche: The non-valley restriction is genuinely three-way because every two-coordinate projection of \(\mathcal U_L\) is the unrestricted square even though triples satisfying \(u_0>u_1\) and \(u_2>u_1\) are deleted. This geometry admits two complementary endpoint routes: canonical joint-polytope facets expose the exact three-normal sparsity, while the direct finite transport dual encodes the forbidden cells and evaluates scalar endpoints using five disjoint prefix/suffix regions. The latter computation is available without first solving the all-\(L\) facet-enumeration problem.
project_justification.fill: The proved endpoint layer supplies the direct legal-incidence primal and dual, an \(O(L)\) exact separator for each dual feasibility query, sparse sharp facet formulas, a fixed-\(L\) global Lipschitz constant, and the explicit \(\pi_{\min}\)-dependent plug-in rate. The proved inference layer supplies exact simultaneous finite-sample honesty through pilot-region and conditional product-multinomial inversion. The project separately retains two honest open problems: the finite-type, exact-once bounded-register stream for the complete joint facet catalogue and the uniform local quantile argument needed for regular-face Wald equivalence.

body.related_work: Russell (2021) studies continuous functionals of the joint law of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model; that random-set and convex-optimization architecture does not classify the present three-marginal forbidden-support polytope. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) derive cumulative sharp bounds and attaining tables for unrestricted bivariate ordinal couplings only, so there is no sharp transfer to the unique-best indicator after a genuinely three-way support deletion. Kim (2014) incorporates support restrictions in a two-marginal Kantorovich dual. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) give an unrestricted multi-marginal transport identification framework and rates for a quadratic objective; for this indicator loss, unrestricted inclusion yields at most outer bounds unless the forbidden triples are encoded by an extended-cost constrained reduction. The direct legal-incidence dual in \(\text{thm:direct-support-transport-dual}\) proves that reduction here, while the root-\(N\) result is derived from the resulting finite affine endpoint map rather than imported from the quadratic theorem. Chiba (2017) concerns the binary-treatment relative treatment effect, and its exact randomization inference assumes independent potential outcomes. Gabriel, Sachs, and Andreas Kryger Jensen (2024), in ``Sharp Symbolic Nonparametric Bounds for Measures of Benefit in Observational and Imperfect Randomized Studies with Ordinal Outcomes,'' derive symbolic results for binary-exposure confounding and binary-instrument noncompliance designs; those settings do not supply this three-dose forbidden-support geometry. Duarte et al. (2024) provide generic discrete causal optimization and anytime outer bounds, Bonet (2001) is the closest causal-polytope precedent for complete observable facets, and Avis and Fukuda (1996) motivate a duplicate-free predecessor search. Kaido and Ponomarev (2025) study support implications through compatibility graphs, but the present nonregular support also augments vertices with unique-peak coordinates. Cho and Russell (2024), Fang and Santos (2019), and Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) motivate LP, directional, and binding-set inference. Here exact finite-sample honesty is proved directly by least-favourable conditional multinomial inversion; equivalence of its localized scalar side to an efficient Wald interval remains open. Goodwin et al. (2022) provide the randomized three-dose setting, but the proposed analysis is conditional on a prespecified score and an added, clinically unvalidated cross-world unimodality restriction.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The complete all-\(L\) predecessor type set and a \(\mathsf{CHECK}_{2\mathrm{BTAS}}\)-accepted exact-once source remain open; the proved direct transport separator computes scalar endpoints but does not catalogue every canonical joint-polytope facet. The conditional multinomial construction proves finite-sample coverage as a mathematical inversion over compact null slices, including all boundary fallbacks, but a practical exact semialgebraic optimizer may be costly. Most importantly, no uniform Berry--Esseen, least-favourable quantile, and inversion remainder over the shrinking pilot region has yet been proved, so regular-face efficient-Wald equivalence is not claimed.
body.honest_scope: For fixed \(L\), the note proves sharp scalar endpoints by both support-constrained transport and canonical facet projection, proves that three facet normals are sometimes necessary, gives a computable global Lipschitz constant and a \(\pi_{\min}\)-dependent root-\(N\) plug-in rate, and constructs a finite-sample honest simultaneous endpoint rectangle with zero-cell, tie, and empty-arm protection. These results do not solve the all-\(L\) sound, complete, unique bounded-register facet stream, and scalar endpoint computation is explicitly not presented as evidence that the stream exists. The adaptive procedure is not yet shown asymptotically equivalent to an efficient Wald interval on regular faces. The Goodwin et al. example remains an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis: randomization and consistency identify score marginals, but the trial neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality, and no empirical data analysis is claimed.
